title: Ouvia: A User-centered Framework for Measuring Usability of Speech Translation in Real-World Communication Scenarios
abstract: arXiv:2606.06177v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Speech translation (ST) is increasingly adopted in user applications, yet its evaluation largely focuses on decontextualized testbeds and holistic quality, rather than end users' communication needs. We introduce Ouvia, an evaluation framework for measuring user-perceived usability of speech translation outputs in real-world settings. Ouvia focuses on one-to-one communication: an English speaker needs to convey a request to a Portuguese speaker, and the message is automatically translated. Through a custom web app and multi-phase study design, we collect more than 1,750 such interactions in healthcare and everyday situations, mediated by four ST systems, involving speakers from three English dialects and two genders. We find that modern ST serves people only to a limited extent---only around half of interactions are rated as usable---with significant gaps in reported usability across demographic groups. translated_title: Ouvia：一个以用户为中心的、用于衡量真实世界交流场景中语音翻译可用性的评估框架
translated_abstract: 语音翻译（ST）在用户应用中的采用日益广泛，但其评估主要聚焦于脱离实际情境的测试平台和整体质量，而非最终用户的交流需求。我们提出了Ouvia，这是一个用于衡量真实世界环境中用户对语音翻译输出感知可用性的评估框架。Ouvia聚焦于一对一交流场景：一名英语使用者需要向一名葡萄牙语使用者传达请求，信息由系统自动翻译。通过自定义网络应用和多阶段研究设计，我们在医疗保健和日常生活情境中收集了超过1,750次此类交互，这些交互由四个语音翻译系统调节，涉及来自三种英语方言和两种性别的说话者。我们发现，现代语音翻译对人们的帮助程度有限——只有大约一半的交互被评为可用——且不同人口群体之间报告的可用性存在显著差距。此外，在质量指标方面……
tldr: Ouvia是一个以用户为中心的评估框架，通过在真实一对一交流场景中收集超过1,750次交互发现，现代语音翻译仅有约一半的交互被评为可用，且不同人口群体之间存在显著的可用性差距。
en_tdlr: Ouvia is a user-centered evaluation framework that, through over 1,750 real-world one-to-one communication interactions, reveals that modern speech translation is rated usable in only about half of cases, with significant usability gaps across demographic groups.
